title: How much feedback delay can a digital twin's controller tolerate, and does a fixed-step simulator get that margin right?
lede: exact: a fixed-step twin under-reports a PD loop's delay margin by 18.6% at dt = 0.1 s and 1.0% at 5 ms, because the largest stable delay is the largest n with (n + 1/2) dt below the true margin (25 of 25 cases)
summary: Exact eigenvalue study (no sampling) of a PD-controlled double integrator with feedback delay (kp = 4, damping ratio 0.3 to 2). The continuous-time delay margin is 0.19 to 0.37 s from the frequency-domain crossing. A fixed-step simulator that must represent the delay as whole steps reports a smaller margin: for the well-damped case (ζ = 0.7) 18.6% too small at dt = 0.1 s, 7.8% at 0.02 s, 2.3% at 0.01 s and 1.0% at 5 ms. For exact zero-order-hold integration the largest stable delay in steps is the largest n with (n + ½)·dt below the true margin, which held in 25 of 25 (damping, step) cases; explicit Euler, semi-implicit Euler and the exact hold agree to the step except for the lightly damped loop. One plant and controller form, constant integer delay, no measured latency from any real system.
